plan.opening_note: My plan: read the hot paths in training and encoding before touching anything, then make one clear algorithmic or allocation change that keeps outputs byte-identical. I'll avoid scattered micro-edits and anything tied to the benchmark inputs, and I'll only submit if evaluate reports the change as accepted.

@@ -25,2 +25,65 @@
-class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
-
+def _merge_chunk(old, pair, idx, w, k, stats, where, removed):
+    """
+    Return merge(old, pair, idx), or None if pair does not occur in old, and
+    update the weighted pair counts (stats) and the pair -> chunks index
+    (where) of chunk k in place. Only pairs touching a merged occurrence
+    change: their old pair loses w, the new pair with idx gains w (and is the
+    only kind of pair new to the chunk). Decremented pairs go to removed.
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    cnt = old.count(p0)
+    if not cnt:
+        return None
+    n = len(old)
+    last = n - 1
+    index = old.index
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    rapp = removed.append
+    same = p0 == p1
+    new = None
+    s = 0 # start of the not yet copied part of old
+    t = 0 # where to search for the next p0
+    prev = -3 # previous merged position
+    while cnt:
+        j = index(p0, t)
+        cnt -= 1
+        if j < last and old[j+1] == p1:
+            if new is None:
+                new = []
+            stats[pair] -= w
+            if j:
+                a = old[j-1]
+                p = (a, p0)
+                stats[p] -= w
+                rapp(p)
+                # an adjacent previous occurrence leaves idx as left neighbour
+                p = (idx, idx) if prev == j - 2 else (a, idx)
+                stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + w
+                where[p].add(k)
+            if j + 2 < n:
+                c = old[j+2]
+                # if the next occurrence starts right here, its left side
+                # accounts for the pair between the two
+                if not (c == p0 and j + 3 < n and old[j+3] == p1):
+                    p = (p1, c)
+                    stats[p] -= w
+                    rapp(p)
+                    p = (idx, c)
+                    stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + w
+                    where[p].add(k)
+            new.extend(old[s:j])
+            new.append(idx)
+            s = t = j + 2
+            prev = j
+            if same:
+                cnt -= 1 # old[j+1] was an occurrence of p0 too
+        else:
+            t = j + 1
+    if new is None:
+        return None
+    new.extend(old[s:])
+    return new
+
+
+class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
+
